 Is Broadcom (AVGO) Cheap Following Anthropic Financing Risk Concerns?
 November 01, 2026 SI Simply Wall St Broadcom (AVGO) is back in the spotlight after investors focused on its large financing guarantees tied to Anthropic’s AI rack leases, raising fresh questions about credit risk and financial flexibility.
 Over the past year Broadcom’s share price has swung hard with the AI trade, with the stock down about 16.9% on a 90 day share price return and 8.2% over 30 days. The 3 year total shareholder return of roughly 2.8x still reflects very strong longer term compounding.
 Scan how markets are repricing AI risk by lining up Broadcom’s story against our curated list of 54 AI infrastructure stocks .
 Broadcom now trades on roughly 18.7x forward earnings after a sharp reset, with AI upside and Anthropic financing risk pulling in opposite directions. Do current valuation multiples still give buyers more upside or downside risk?
 Advertisement Most Popular Narrative: 50% Undervalued
 Broadcom’s most followed valuation story pegs fair value at about $651 per share, almost double the last close of $326.08. This frames today’s selloff as a valuation gap rather than just AI fatigue.
 Just as utilities, railroads, and industrial suppliers provide essential infrastructure for the physical economy, Broadcom provides essential infrastructure for the digital economy. Whether data is generated by AI models, cloud applications, enterprise software, autonomous systems, or future technologies that do not yet exist, that data must still be processed, moved, connected, secured, and managed. 
 See why 185 investors see Broadcom as 50% undervalued .
 Result: Fair Value of $651.05 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, Broadcom’s Anthropic guarantees and any sharp pullback in hyperscaler AI spending could quickly challenge the idea that this stock is simply mispriced infrastructure.
